plans.objective: Build both revisions (buggy 65a2a749773a and fixed) with the same compiled recipe so pandas' Cython extensions compile against the era-appropriate NumPy, then run the developer test selected with -k plus the file path on each side. Only the environment is changed; T_dev is untouched.

assumptions: The harness default CPython is compatible with this pandas revision (pandas 3.x era requires Python >= 3.11); python_version left unset because the context does not state one and the current interpreter was not checked.
PR date is not stated; no pins are applied, so NumPy and scipy resolve to the newest releases (inferred from the unbounded constraints).

scipy is listed as numerically relevant from issue#62946 but is not pinned or installed explicitly; if the developer test imports scipy and it is missing, the buggy side would fail at import rather than on the numerical assertion.
The -k selector with the file path is used because the case may be a class method; the class name is not given in the context.

actions.step: Build buggy revision as a compiled package (Cython extensions in pandas/_libs) in its own venv, default interpreter, no pins: NumPy and scipy are unbounded in the evidence, so the newest compatible release is used and this choice is stated in assumptions.
Build fixed revision with the same recipe so the comparison is like for like.
Run the developer test on buggy; expect a real assertion failure (wrong large skew value where NaN is expected), not a collection or import error.
Run the same developer test on fixed; expect PASS.

plans.success_criterion: The selected test fails on buggy with an assertion failure from the rolling skew/kurtosis computation and passes on fixed, with both revisions built by the same compiled recipe and neither failing at setup or collection.
